firstInjuryRoutine.scope: Only source kind 65 with timer 1..63 and life byte exactly 1; one source actor-update tick, not one display frame
firstInjuryRoutine.terminalTransition: At timer 1 the next source update produces kind 17, timer 0 and life byte 0; other player/global fields and game-over paths remain unmodeled

limits: Each 600-frame run matches the unmodified emulator's individual RAM/screen hashes and the pure contact predicate's individual source returns. Kind 65 occupies exactly 66 frames before the first life-byte decrement in these three cases; kind 64 occupies one or two frames, and the second contact follows a different kind sequence. These observations do not establish the full injury algorithm, lives interpretation, game-over screen, attack damage, respawn or native enemy AI.
